a:r.a:t: Multivalent Adapter Proteins Allow Modular and Adaptable Signal Transduction

p:cNvPr.descr: Illustrations of some binding modules of signaling proteins. Each protein is represented by a line, with the amino terminus to the left, and symbols indicate the location of conserved binding domains. From top to bottom, the first is adaptor, which is a line with three downward-facing kidney structures strung on like beads. The first and third kidneys are blue and lableded SH3; the second is purple and labeled SH2. At the end of the line, the structure is labeled Grb2. Next, another module is adaptor. It is similar in arrangement as the first one; however, there are only two shapes – the first is a purple diamond-shaped PTB, and the second is SH2. The end of the line is labeled Shc. The third one is kinase. The three structures here are SH3, SH2, and a white rectangle with green outlines labeled Tyr kinase. At the end of that, the line is labeled Src. Fourth, there is phosphotase, which is two SH2 strung to a another rectangle labeled Tyr phosphatase in a box with green outline. That line is labeled Shp2. The next one is Ras signaling. This structure is much more complex than the others; it is a combination of SH2, SH3, and SH2, connected to a light brown hexagon labeled PH, a green circle labeled C2, and a rectangle with a green outline labeled GTPase-activating. This line is labeled RasGAP. Next, is transcription. The first structure is a blue rectangular box labeled DNA, which is connected to SH2 and a blue square box labeled TA. The end of the line is labeled STAT. The next one is signal regulation. This is SH2 connected to a yellow box labeled SOCS. The end of the line is also labeled SOCS. Finally, there’s another complex structure labeled “Phospholipid second messenger signaling.” This is a PH connected to a rectangular box with green outline labeled PLC, half the shape of PH, two SH2s, SH3, another half shape of a PH, another PLC, and a C2. This is labeled PLC gamma. To the top right, there is a table labeled “Binding targets.” The first one is a structure that resembles SH3, but is labeled Proline-rich protein or membrane lipid PIP3. The next one is similar to the SH2 structure, but is labeled Tyr-P. The next one is a purple diamond labeled Tyr-P as well, followed by a structure that looks like PH, but is labeled PIP3. The next one is a structure that looks like C2, but is labeled Phospholipids (Ca2+-dependent), followed by a blue rectangle labeled DNA and a light blue square labeled Transcriptional activation, and a yellow rectangle labeled Carboxyl-terminal domain marking protein for attachment of ubiquitin.

p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram C. A vertical diagram begins with the word Signal on top with a down arrow pointing to three yellow circles connected by two lines arranged in the shape of the letter V. The vertex of the V is connected by a line down to a circle labeled P which sits inside a green oval with a cutout to hold the circle. The oval is connected by a line down to a circle labeled P, which sits inside of a pink rectangle with a cutout to hold the cirle. Below this rectangle is an arrow down to the word Response. The text accompanying the diagram reads, "Modularity. Proteins with multivarlent affinities form diverse signaling complexes from interchangable parts. Phosphorylation provides reversible points of interaction."
